content: The provided text is a detailed list of drug interactions, primarily focusing on how calcium carbonate, magnesium hydroxide, and other agents affect the absorption, bioavailability, or pharmacodynamic effects of various medications. 1. Magnesium hydroxide reduces the effectiveness of chloroquine by binding cations in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract, thereby inhibiting its absorption. To mitigate this, doses should be separated by at least 4 hours. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Magnesium hydroxide decreases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction is specific to oral formulations. Ciprofloxacin should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium hydroxide. Co-administration with multivalent cation-containing products can reduce ciprofloxacin bioavailability by up to 90%. Close monitoring is advised. 3. Calcium carbonate reduces ciprofloxacin absorption in the GI tract, leading to decreased effectiveness. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Ciprofloxacin should be taken 2 hours before or 6 hours after calcium salts. Monitoring is recommended. 4. Calcium carbonate antagonizes the pharmacodynamic effects of clevidipine, potentially reducing its efficacy. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Magnesium hydroxide decreases crizotinib levels by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility and bioavailability. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Although no formal studies have been conducted, caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. Calcium carbonate similarly reduces crizotinib levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Drugs that elevate gastric pH may decrease crizotinib solubility and bioavailability. Monitoring is advised. 7. Calcium carbonate reduces cyclosporine levels by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Doses should be separated by at least 2 hours. Monitoring is recommended. 8. Calcium carbonate decreases dabrafenib levels by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility and bioavailability. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Drugs that alter upper GI tract pH, such as proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), H2 blockers, or antacids, may reduce dabrafenib bioavailability. Monitoring is advised. 9. Magnesium hydroxide reduces deferiprone levels by enhancing its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 10. Calcium carbonate also reduces deferiprone levels by enhancing GI absorption. Deferiprone may bind polyvalent cations (e.g., iron, aluminum, zinc). Administration should be separated by at least 4 hours between deferiprone and other medications or supplements containing these cations. Close monitoring is advised. 11. Deferoxamine decreases calcium carbonate levels by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Deferoxamine chelates iron, but its affinity for other minerals is unknown. Monitoring is recommended. 12. Magnesium hydroxide and deflazacort both lower serum potassium levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Calcium carbonate reduces delafloxacin levels by binding cations in the GI tract. Oral delafloxacin forms chelate with alkaline earth and transition metal cations. Administration should be separated by at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. 14. Calcium carbonate increases dextroamphetamine levels by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Monitoring is recommended. 15. Calcium carbonate increases digoxin effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution and monitoring are advised. 16. Calcium carbonate reduces diltiazem effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitoring is recommended. 17. Magnesium hydroxide reduces dolutegravir levels by binding cations in the GI tract. Dolutegravir should be administered 2 hours before or 6 hours after medications containing polyvalent cations. Alternative therapies should be considered if available. Monitoring is recommended. 18. Calcium carbonate similarly reduces dolutegravir levels by cation binding in the GI tract. Administration should be separated by 2 hours (for dolutegravir or abacavir/dolutegravir/lamivudine) or 4 hours (for dolutegravir/rilpivirine) before or 6 hours after polyvalent cation-containing medications. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is advised. 19. Calcium carbonate reduces elvitegravir levels by forming ionic complexes in the GI tract, not by altering gastric pH. Doses should be separated by at least 2 hours. Monitoring is recommended. 20. Magnesium hydroxide reduces fleroxacin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Doses should be separated by 2 hours. Monitoring is recommended. 21. Calcium carbonate reduces levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting GI absorption. Doses should be separated by 2 hours. Monitoring is recommended. 22. Calcium carbonate reduces enalapril effects through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Monitoring is recommended. 23. Calcium carbonate increases ephedrine levels by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Monitoring is recommended. 24. Calcium carbonate increases erythromycin levels (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate forms) through an unknown mechanism. Monitoring is recommended. 25. Calcium carbonate reduces esmolol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Doses should be separated by 2 hours. Monitoring is recommended. 26. Calcium carbonate reduces estramustine levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Estramustine should be taken with water at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals. Monitoring is recommended. 27. Calcium carbonate reduces etidronate levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Doses should be separated by 30 minutes. Monitoring is recommended. 28. Calcium carbonate reduces felodipine effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitoring is recommended. 29. Calcium carbonate reduces ferric maltol levels by increasing gastric pH. Monitoring is recommended. 30. Calcium carbonate reduces ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, and ferrous sulfate levels by increasing gastric pH. Monitoring is recommended. 31. Calcium carbonate increases flecainide levels by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Monitoring is recommended. 32. Calcium carbonate reduces fosamprenavir levels by increasing gastric pH. Monitoring is recommended. 33. Calcium carbonate reduces fosinopril effects through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Monitoring is recommended. 34. Calcium carbonate reduces gabapentin and gabapentin enacarbil levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Doses should be separated by 2 hours. Monitoring is recommended. 35. Calcium carbonate reduces gefitinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Doses should be separated by at least 6 hours. Monitoring is recommended. 36. Magnesium hydroxide reduces gemifloxacin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Doses should be separated by 2 hours. Monitoring is recommended. 37. Calcium carbonate increases glipizide and glyburide levels by increasing gastric pH. Monitoring is recommended. 38. Calcium carbonate reduces ibandronate levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Doses should be separated by 30 minutes. Monitoring is recommended. 39. Calcium carbonate reduces isoniazid levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Doses should be separated by 2 hours. Monitoring is recommended. 40. Calcium carbonate reduces itraconazole levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Acid-neutralizing medications should be administered at least 2 hours before or after itraconazole. Monitoring is recommended. 41. Calcium carbonate reduces ketoconazole levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Doses should be separated by 2 hours. Monitoring is recommended. 42. Calcium carbonate reduces labetalol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Doses should be separated by 2 hours. Monitoring is recommended. 43. Calcium carbonate reduces levothyroxine levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Administration should be separated by 4 hours. Monitoring is recommended. 44. Calcium carbonate increases lisdexamfetamine levels by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Monitoring is recommended. 45. Calcium carbonate reduces lisinopril effects through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Monitoring is recommended. 46. Calcium carbonate increases memantine levels by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Monitoring is recommended. 47. Calcium carbonate reduces methscopolamine levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Monitoring is recommended. 48. Calcium carbonate reduces methylphenidate effects by enhancing GI absorption. For extended-release capsules (e.g., Ritalin LA), co-administration with antacids or acid suppressants may alter drug release. Consider separating administration. Monitoring is recommended. 49. Calcium carbonate reduces metoprolol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Doses should be separated by 2 hours. Monitoring is recommended. 50. Calcium carbonate increases mexiletine levels by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Monitoring is recommended. 51. Calcium carbonate reduces moexipril effects through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Monitoring is recommended. 52. Calcium carbonate reduces mycophenolate levels by increasing gastric pH. Monitoring is recommended. 53. Calcium carbonate reduces nadolol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Doses should be separated by 2 hours. Monitoring is recommended. 54. Calcium carbonate reduces nebivolol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Doses should be separated by 2 hours. Monitoring is recommended. 55. Calcium carbonate reduces neratinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Doses should be separated by 3 hours. Monitoring is recommended. 56. Calcium carbonate reduces nifedipine and nicardipine effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitoring is recommended. 57. Calcium carbonate reduces nilotinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Antacids should be administered 2 hours before or after nilotinib. Monitoring is recommended. 58. Calcium carbonate reduces nitrofurantoin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Doses should be separated by 2 hours. Monitoring is recommended.
